findings.explanation: 2 cookie(s) classified as requiring consent were stored before any interaction with the page: _ga (Google Analytics, analytics, first-party) and _late_tag (Fixture Tracker, marketing, first-party). Art. 5(3) requires prior consent for storing information on the visitor's device unless it is strictly necessary for a service the visitor requested.

1 known tracking service(s) were contacted before any interaction with the page: Fixture Tracker (tracker.test, first request at 0.0 s). The EDPB considers that sending information from the device through tracking pixels and URLs falls within Art. 5(3) and requires prior consent unless an exemption applies.

2 Web Storage key(s) written before any interaction look like identifiers or come from third parties and could not be classified: _pk_id (localStorage of http://site.test:40693) and widget_visitor (localStorage of http://widget.test:40693). Their purpose has to be checked.
A consent interface was detected on the page (unidentified platform; controls recognised: accept, reject).
The first layer of the consent interface offers a refusal option (“Tout refuser”) alongside acceptance (“Tout accepter”).

1 analytics cookie(s) stored before consent have a lifetime above 13 months: _ga (13.1 months (400 days)). A site relying on the CNIL audience-measurement exemption is expected to limit tracker lifetime, for example to thirteen months (French guidance). The browser used caps cookie lifetimes at 400 days, so the lifetime set by the site may be even longer.
This point cannot be established by observing the website from outside. It is listed so a reviewer can examine it.
